PE:
•	 Students will be provided laboratory coats in cases where biohazards will be present. 
Laboratory coats are only to be worn in the laboratory and removed before leaving the 
laboratory. For example: do not leave the laboratory to go to the restroom while wearing 
a laboratory coat.
•	 Appropriately sized gloves are to be worn on both hands. Gloves are to be removed 
before touching computers, cell phones, and other items that could become contaminated. 
As with laboratory coats, gloves are to be removed before leaving the laboratory.
•	 The removal and disposal of gloves  
Figure 1.3: Sequence for the safe removal of gloves. 
Taken from the online PDF “Sequence for Putting on 
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)”. Centers for 
Disease Control and Prevention.
(Figure 1.3):
•	 Step 1: Roll glove off of one hand 
so that it is inside out.
•	 Step 2: Place that glove in the palm 
of the remaining gloved hand
•	 Step 3: Roll glove off second hand 
so that the second glove is inside 
out with the first glove inside it.
•	 Step 4: Dispose of gloves in red-
bag lined biohazard bin
3.	 Procedures for handling and disposing of 
biohazards:
•	 Gloves and laboratory coats are to be 
worn whenever biohazards are to be 
handled. 

13 
L A B O R A T O R Y 1
•	 Students may handle lancets used to stick their own fingers without gloves.
•	 Students will wear gloves to handle microcuvettes and other non-sharps for analysis of 
blood samples collected in the lab. Demonstrations of proper handling of biohazards 
will occur before laboratory activities take place.
